subject: Unexpected hourly aggregation in AWS marketplace invoice — multi-account attribution
messages:
From: ApexCloud Solutions <billing@apexcloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Spike on April invoice — suspect multi-account hourly aggregation

Diego,

We pulled our April AWS Marketplace invoice and are seeing a ~48% jump vs. our internal metering. The invoice appears to have aggregated hourly windows across three linked AWS accounts into single line items; our internal tooling reports per-minute meters. The attached sample (apex_metered_lines.csv) shows the lines we think are wrong — same OfferID, but quantities that look like hourly sums rather than per-minute ingestion. Can Redwood confirm whether your marketplace submission pipeline does any hourly rollups before reporting?

What we need from you:
- Confirmation of the billing window used by Redwood when you submit usage to AWS Marketplace.
- Per-offer mapping from Redwood SKU -> Marketplace OfferID for our account.
- Any reconciliation guidance you can share so we can reconcile your invoice to our internal usage.

Attachments: apex_metered_lines.csv (CSV, ~1.6MB)

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Billing Operations
ApexCloud Solutions
[Attachment: apex_metered_lines.csv (CSV, 1.6MB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike on April invoice — suspect multi-account hourly aggregation

Lena / Apex team —

Thanks for the heads up and for the CSV; I pulled it down. I’m looping in Marissa (Sales Ops) and Rafael (Finance) to own the invoice-level trace. A few quick clarifying points from our side:

- Redwood submits usage to AWS Marketplace on a per-usage-record basis; we do not intentionally aggregate multiple accounts into a single line, but the Marketplace API accepts hourly windows and some partners submit aggregated hourly totals.
- We need to map the OfferIDs in your CSV to Redwood internal SKUs and the Redwood-origin account IDs so we can trace ingestion timestamps.
- We’ll also check whether our ingestion client did any window alignment (UTC vs account local time) that could cause apparent doubling when multiple linked accounts are consolidated by the seller.

Action items I’m tracking:
1) Marissa to pull the SKU->OfferID mapping and share HubSpot deal reference.
2) Rafael to run a quick per-offer delta sample and attach a short calc.
3) I’ll request the raw ingestion logs and a short reconciliation note (initial_recon_notes.md) and share back.

Please confirm if you can also provide a matched sample of the AWS usage record IDs (URIs) for the suspect lines — that speeds tracing on our side.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Lead 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_recon_notes.md (text)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcloud.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike on April invoice — suspect multi-account hourly aggregation

Lena / team —

Adding the mapping we use on our side. The HubSpot deal (link below) lists the seller mapping and our internal SKU names. In several past reconciliation cases the mismatch came from sellers reporting an hourly rollup where we expected per-minute granularity; that creates an apparent surge if two linked accounts overlap the same hour.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/6789/deal/DEAL-APX-2027-03
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/invoice/APX-2027-03

I’ve attached a short text export of the hubspot object (hubspot-6789.txt) for your records. Rafael — take a look at the OfferID 333-APX-STD in the CSV — previously this SKU had a known hourly bundling flag in our mapping table; we may need to request a corrected invoice from the seller.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hubspot-6789.txt]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike on April invoice — suspect multi-account hourly aggregation

Team —

I pulled a small sample and ran a quick delta between Apex's CSV and our aggregated ingestion logs. Summary:

- Line example: OfferID 333-APX-STD, invoice line qty = 43,200; our per-minute sum across the three linked accounts = 14,400.
- Hypothesis: Marketplace ingestion window aligned to the hour and then summed per-account hourly totals rather than raw per-minute events, effectively tripling the quantity in cases where the accounts had overlapping flow at the same hour.
- Financial impact for April (pre-VAT): ~$18,200 overcharge on that OfferID alone. With VAT included (Apex is EU-registered) the gross variance is larger.

I attached a calc sample (calc_sample.xlsx) showing the math (sheet: sample-delta). Proposed remediation: request seller reissue corrected invoice lines OR ask marketplace to split the hourly aggregate back into per-minute granularity where possible. I recommend we:

1) Request corrected invoice from Apex (seller) for the affected OfferIDs.
2) If seller cannot reissue, request an official Marketplace adjustment (invoice credit) referencing the URIs for the usage records.

Lena — can you confirm if Apex can generate corrected per-minute usage exports? If not, we’ll start the formal request with AWS Marketplace Support (cc'd).

Rafael Mendes
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: calc_sample.xlsx (XLSX, stub)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@apexcloud.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike on April invoice — suspect multi-account hourly aggregation

Thanks all — good progress. Quick summary / action plan so we have one record: 

- Root cause (likely): Seller-side hourly rollup across linked accounts accepted by Marketplace ingestion window alignment. This doubled/tripled quantities for overlapping hours.
- Short term: Apex to try to furnish per-minute usage export. If delivered, Rafael will reconcile and we will ask for corrected invoice reissue.
- If seller cannot provide per-minute data, we (Redwood) will escalate to AWS Marketplace Support to request an invoice adjustment referencing the URIs and our calc sample.
- Tax/VAT note: Rafael — if Apex reissues, ensure corrected invoice includes original VAT breakdown; if Marketplace issues credit, confirm whether VAT is handled in the marketplace credit memo or via seller paperwork.

Karthik — please keep an eye on ingestion client version used for April (release v3.4.1) and flag any time-window alignment behavior; if we detect an upload-side bug we need a fast post-mortem.

Lena — can you ack receipt and confirm ETA to provide per-minute exports (or confirm they cannot be produced)? If ETA over 5 business days, Rafael and I will open the AWS support case.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Lead 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_reconciliation_request.pdf (PDF, stub)]
